current.text: LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges are gone. Naz Reid, Royce O'Neale and Grayson Allen came in, and Coby White is there for a full season.
The team still needs to waive three players. The Hield-for-Dillingham trade was made to lower the cost of those cuts.
Projected starters are White, Knueppel, Miller, Reid and Diabaté. Reid starts at power forward, and White starts over Dennis Schröder.
Grayson Allen starts while Knueppel is out. He would also start if Miller misses games early in the season.
The projected bench is Allen, Schröder, Steinbach, O'Neale and Grant Williams.
Losing Ball and Bridges opens a lot of usage. White and Knueppel are the main players expected to gain usage.
There is no clear lead creator. Playmaking should be spread across White, Knueppel and Miller, and how the ball gets split will shape their efficiency.
There is no trusted backup point guard on the roster.
The center plan is unclear. Diabaté, the rookie taken 14th and Kalkbrenner all compete for the job. The team was better last season with Diabaté starting.
Center minutes will likely be split three ways. Grant Williams also plays as a small-ball five. No center is likely to get near 30 minutes.
Bridges leaving frees about 32 minutes in the four and five mix. The crowded frontcourt, with Diabaté, Kalkbrenner and Kai Jones, limits Reid's minutes at center.
Coach Charles Lee is expected to try different frontcourt lineups. Starters should stay stable, but closing lineups will change by matchup.
The team is going all in on spacing and will take a lot of threes. It also stresses steals and offensive rebounds.
Without Ball, Charlotte lost the passer who drove its transition play. Its defense may be very bad.
The roster is deep. The team is more likely a play-in team than an outright playoff team. Its win total of 37.5 ranks 20th of 30.
Charlotte has a 40 million USD trade exception and could add a player at the trade deadline.
Charlotte has only 13 back-to-backs, the fewest in the league, so rest risk for its starters is low.
The playoff schedule is 4-3-4 games for our March 28 end, 11 in total, which ranks 4th of 30. Weeks 20 and 21 have no back-to-backs.
Charlotte plays only two games in the week starting March 1, which is the last week before our playoffs.

durable.text: The Hornets have been cautious with their stars' health. Some missed games by their star have been tied to tanking.
Charlotte does not let its centers shoot threes. Kalkbrenner did not shoot them last season, and Steinbach was not allowed to shoot in Summer League.

tags.name: good playoff schedule
tags.detail: 4-3-4 in weeks 19 to 21, 11 games, rank 4 of 30. Only one back-to-back, in week 19.

tags.name: deep rotation
tags.detail: Deep roster that still has to waive three players. Minutes are spread, mostly in the frontcourt.
tags.new_meaning: The team has many playable players, so minutes are spread out and few players get heavy loads.

tags.name: center committee
tags.detail: Diabaté, Kalkbrenner and the rookie taken 14th share the center minutes, with Grant Williams at small-ball five.
tags.new_meaning: Several centers share the minutes at center, so none of them gets a full starter's load.

tags.name: three-point heavy
tags.detail: Built around spacing, takes a lot of threes. Centers are not allowed to shoot them.
tags.new_meaning: The team takes many threes as a style, which lifts 3PTM for its perimeter shooters.

note: Charlotte loses Ball and Bridges, so White, Knueppel, Miller and Reid all move up in usage. With so few back-to-backs and an 11-game playoff schedule, they are safe starters to roster through week 21. The centers lose value because three of them share the job, and Allen gains value while Knueppel and Miller are injured. Early on, watch who takes over the ball handling, who wins the starting center job, and how the team handles the weak two-game week starting March 1.
